output.summary: A deciduous tree native to the eastern United States, commonly occurring in floodplains and swamps. Young bark peels in thin, curling salmon-pink to brown-grey layers, becoming darker, thicker and deeply furrowed with age. Unlike most birches, its fruit matures in late spring.
output.edibilityNote: Native Americans used boiled sap as a maple-like sweetener and ate the inner bark as survival food.
